speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: asked	the Minister for Finance (a) whether there are guidelines given to Ministries or Statutory Boards to ensure (i) clauses in Government tender specifications for service contracts are fair to service providers and (ii) liquidated damages commensurate with the non-delivery of service; (b) whether there are avenues for service providers to flag out unfair or one-sided clauses in tender specifications; (c) whether there is training given to Government procurement officers to ensure fair contracts; and (d) whether an audit can be conducted on Government tender contracts to ensure fair clauses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Agencies can choose to use these templates or adapt them accordingly to cater to their specific unique needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: From time to time, these templates are reviewed, taking into account feedback that we receive and any appropriate industrial norms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: There are also contracts which do not impose liquidated damages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Whatever the case, Government agencies are advised to work closely with their contractors to resolve issues early.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: However, it is not possible for training to cover every scenario on what is fair or unfair, or every type of purchase that Government agencies make.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The Government buys a wide variety of goods and services, and each industry has differing practices and norms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: What is considered the norm and reasonable in one industry may not be so in another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: For example, in the creative design industry, the industry norm allows up to three rounds of consolidated changes after the design concept has been signed off.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: But this does not apply to architecture design of buildings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: For example, we work with Building and Construction Authority (BCA) for the procurement of construction services and Infocomm Development Authority of Singapore (IDA) for procurement of IT services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Today, every agency which intends to procure services or products will indicate the agency's contact person's details in the GeBIZ procurement notice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: I would encourage suppliers who have any questions about a specific tender or quotation, whether on the tender specifications or contractual terms and conditions, to contact the agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Where the questions or concerns pertain to an agency's procurement practice, suppliers can also raise these to the agency's Quality Service Manager.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Apart from these channels, suppliers may also give their feedback on government procurement matters to MOF's Quality Service Manager or on the GeBIZ feedback page.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: First, what can the Government do to encourage fair and reasonable outsourced contracts in the private sector?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Second, can the Government consider setting up a body similar to the Consumer Association of Singapore (CASE) to help mediate should there be any contractual disputes between service buyers and service providers?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is a little difficult for the Government to step into that arena, as it were.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What one would have to rely on are the general principles of contracts.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is obviously bargaining power; that is one of the things that you take into account.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If it contravenes the Unfair Contract Terms Act, then, obviously, certain things will not be enforced.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is a matter of general law and that has developed over time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With respect to the other question of a body to encourage mediation, in fact, we do have the Singapore Mediation Centre.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It hears not just international cases but also domestic cases as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I agree with the Member that mediation or amicable resolution is something to be encouraged.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are tribunals where you can take your cases for mediation.
